title: UK Biobank whole-genome sequencing reveals robust contributions of rare variants to complex-trait heritability.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Data availability statement (via paper_context.py); Zenodo record 10.5281/zenodo.19378367 file listing (one 5,243-byte code zip, no data); unzipped the Europe PMC supplement: two PDFs (204 KB Tables S1–S12, 278 KB Figs S1–S2) plus figure images, no tabular data files.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: 348,977 participants, 5,378,300 rare variants, five traits and their heritability estimates (0.37 height, 0.15 BMI, etc.); statement that individual-level data need a UK Biobank application (ID 83990).

a1_downloadable.note: Individual-level whole-genome sequencing and phenotypes are UK Biobank controlled access (application required). Public material is only code (5 KB Zenodo zip) and PDF summary tables; checked both.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Public output is about five heritability estimates in PDF tables, not a per-item label column; trait values exist only in controlled UK Biobank data.

a3_inputs_present.note: Genotypes are not public; only referenced via UK Biobank.

a4_units_stated.note: Heritability is a unitless proportion; not relevant given A1 failure.

a5_enough_rows.note: Public summary tables cover 5 traits across a few subsets/sensitivity analyses; far below 1,500 rows. Row count of PDF tables not tallied.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: Hundreds of GB to TB (whole-genome sequencing of ~349,000 people)
a6_fits_laptop.note: Even with access, the genotype working set is far beyond a laptop; the paper used GCTA and BOLT-REML (mixed-model software) on a cluster-scale resource.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not checkable without access; no conflicting counts seen.

a8_label_provenance.note: Traits (height, BMI, platelet count, blood pressure, HbA1c) are physical measurements; not the blocker.

honest_claim_h3: No ML claim possible from public data: only five trait-level heritability estimates are released; the individual-level data require a UK Biobank application.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a person's rare DNA variants to predict measured traits like height and body mass index.
plain_idea.train_on: Whole-genome rare variants for each of ~349,000 UK Biobank participants (count from the paper; data controlled-access, not opened).
plain_idea.predict: Measured height, BMI (body mass index), platelet count, systolic blood pressure and HbA1c (glycated haemoglobin, a blood sugar marker), recorded at UK Biobank assessment visits.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Would show how much rare variants add to trait prediction beyond common-variant polygenic scores, but the data cannot be obtained without an access application.

ml_idea: Rare-variant burden plus polygenic score to predict quantitative traits; infeasible: controlled-access, TB-scale genotypes.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; data are controlled access and genome-scale.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Data availability statement: UK Biobank application required — already fails.

verdict_reason: A1 fails: individual-level genomes and traits are UK Biobank controlled access (application required); public outputs are only code and PDF tables of five heritability estimates, and the genotype data would be far too large for a laptop anyway.
